name: Gilt market
summary: Gilt yields steady near 5.15% after the Bank of England's first rate rise since 2023
state: The 10-year gilt yield fell toward 5.1% early on 6 Nov, its lowest since late August, before edging back above 5.15%, after the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov (Trading Economics). Markets price three more rises by November 2027. No weak auction or BoE intervention has been reported, and Watch is kept while yields stay near multi-year highs.
for_you: Fixed mortgage rates track gilt yields; lenders may reprice deals after the Bank Rate rise. Describes market conditions only; it is not advice.
rubric_hit: Gilt yields near multi-year highs after a BoE hike; no intervention = Watch (kept)

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK gilt yields fall as flight to safety offsets hawkish BoE
Bank of England — Interest rates and Bank Rate

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
